Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but VRTX books $20mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000875320-26-000056), 0.17% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -0.17%. Restated without working capital build: over 2021 to 2025 VRTX's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,164mm, inventories up $1,594mm, payables up $288mm, a working capital build of $2,470mm, 5.00% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -0.17% where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.72%, and stays there.
